answer: An agent network can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed when independent audits show it fabricated work or colluded to collect rewards. Audits sample tasks and compare outputs against hidden tests; repeated identities cannot cheaply multiply influence, because every new account needs capital at risk and a history of passing checks. The bond might be called ivory, while a willow and a quill label test cases; the names change nothing. The attacker pays for each Sybil and risks losing its stake.
